Theme

Work & responsibility · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Money, work & business

incentive noun

also incentives, inducement, motive (an incentive), stimulus, spur

classical

Cic. Arch. 23: et perīculōrum et labōrum (Lewis & Short)
Tac. A. 2.38: incitāmentum Tiberiō fuit

incitāmentum, incitāmentī n.

noun, second declension; with genitive or ad

incentive, inducement, spur

Whatever spurs someone on: glory, a reward, an example; in Tacitus also of a person who urges on (incitāmentum mortis).

Other words

  • invītāmentum, invītāmentī n. — an inducement, an attraction

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 10.10.2 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 2.42.6: temeritātis

    Something that draws one on, an invitation to act: Cicero sets an honour that is an invītāmentum ad tempus against one that is the reward of lasting merit (below).

  • stimulus, stimulī m. — a goad, a spur

    noun, second declension · also used · classical

    The ox-goad, and figuratively whatever pricks one on, as in English.

  • praemium, praemiī n. — a reward (offered as an incentive)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical

    Where the incentive is a prize or a payment (see reward).

Examples

  • is autem nōn invītāmentum ad tempus, sed perpetuae virtūtis praemium

    an honour that is no passing inducement, but the reward of lasting meritCic. Fam. 10.10.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • inclīnātiō senātūs incitāmentum Tiberiō fuit quō prōmptius adversārētur

    the senate’s leaning was an incentive to Tiberius to oppose him the more readilyTac. A. 2.38 (Lewis & Short)

See also reward, encourage.
